title: No release path leaves a story unreachable (#877)

story.i_want_to: every claim release on a delivery story to end somewhere the driver or a human acts on
story.so_that: a crashed or refused dispatch never silently drops its story out of the loop

rationale: Every caller of Stages.follow_release/5 leaves agent_status pending at stage queued, and the driver selects contracted stories only, so the story sits unreachable with no alert. The disposition has to depend on the cause, which the release paths do not currently carry: a refusal is free to retry, a crash costs money, and an operator's release is a human decision. The retry ceiling is spend, so it has no default.

acceptance_criteria.description: force_unclaim_story/3 accepts release_cause: :placement_refused | :attempt | :operator (default :operator), and Placement.undo_claim/5 passes :placement_refused when the runner was unavailable (not connected, at capacity, a lock not granted) or the placement lost a race (stale claim epoch, a dispatch already replied to or already in the ledger, a runner no longer authorized) and :attempt for a refusal that recurs every pass (a payload the contract rejects, a story it could not attach).
A :placement_refused release leaves the story queued and contracted.
A lease reclaim or a counted US-44.3 release with fewer than DISPATCH_MAX_ATTEMPTS counted releases leaves the story queued and contracted.
A lease reclaim or counted release that reaches the ceiling takes {queued, escalated, :attempts_exhausted} with the count in escalation_reason.
With DISPATCH_MAX_ATTEMPTS unset, the first counted release takes {queued, escalated, :attempts_exhausted}.
A verifier-reject auto-reset or bulk reject of a story whose stage row is in flight counts toward the ceiling and follows the same rule.
An :operator force-unclaim of a delivery story takes {queued, escalated, :operator_released}.
A story with no delivery stage row is released exactly as today.

test_cases.name: placement refusal re-contracts
steps: DispatchDriver places it; runner replies refused

test_cases.name: crash under the ceiling retries
preconditions: config/test.exs sets the max-attempts key to 2
claimed delivery story past its lease
expected_results: stage queued, agent_status contracted, attempts runner_lost 1

test_cases.name: ceiling reached escalates through the worker
preconditions: story whose attempts runner_lost is 1, claimed past its lease
expected_results: stage escalated, edge attempts_exhausted, count 2 in reason

test_cases.name: unset ceiling escalates on the first release
preconditions: the config reader over a config with no max-attempts key
steps: read the ceiling; decide for one counted release

test_cases.name: in-flight reject counts
preconditions: story reported done under a dispatch, row at ci
expected_results: queued and contracted under the ceiling; counted

test_cases.name: non-delivery story untouched
preconditions: claimed story with no stage row
expected_results: agent_status pending as today; no stage row

technical_notes: follow_release/5 callers: progress.ex:1189, :1637, :2931, :3601; bulk_operations.ex:610. force_unclaim_multi and the reject auto-reset both pass :claim_released today, so the cause must be threaded in

Counting: Stages.transition_update already counts attempts per edge (stages.ex:1080-1093); the ceiling counts runner_lost plus claim_released from in-flight rejects, the claimant's own unclaim (a session that always gives the story back must not loop for ever, and sending it to a human is not a custody bypass) and a placement refusal that recurs every pass; never a placement the runner was unavailable for, or an operator release
A reject whose row is past ci (merged, deployed) only rebinds the row (stages.ex:984-988); that path keeps today's behaviour and is out of scope

Re-contract as a guarded pending -> contracted step inside the release's own transaction (Progress.recontract_in_transaction/3), writing the audit entry and webhook contract_story/4 writes from the same builders; contract_story/4 itself is unchanged
New control-only edges {queued, escalated, :attempts_exhausted} and {queued, escalated, :operator_released} in StageMachine and the contract
DISPATCH_MAX_ATTEMPTS: row in deploy/FLY_SECRETS.md, no default; one reader function used by runtime config and by the worker, so the unset case is tested through the same reader the worker calls
Tests never Application.put_env; the configured value in config/test.exs is 2
non_goals: Does not change the lease length (US-44.5)
Does not change post-merge reject behaviour
Does not add alerting beyond the escalated queue
